chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: How he came to record with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Mitchell was called in when Morton's planned men fell through; Allen relays that Morton rated him above Armstrong and Simeon as clarinet favorite.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about those Jelly Roll Martin recordings. So many people, including me, think they're about the greatest records that we ever heard, the greatest ever made. If you could tell us about when you first met Jelly Roll, and how you started to play with him, and made some of those records.

Oh, well, uh, with Jelly, I don't know how I got started with Jelly. Let's see. It, uh, you see, I was working on a study job, around here at that time. And Jelly, he was recording. And, uh, I think, uh, one time there, something happened that he couldn't, the fellas that he had, uh, planned on using, why they, I don't know where, what happened. But, he, uh, they, they didn't work out. And, so you know how you have to do and you have to scout around and get someone. So that's the way I got started with Jelly. And, uh, he called me and, uh, uh, I'd come down to rehearsal and make some recordings. And, of course, there's a little extra money, you know. And, I'd, uh, run down and make his...

Had you played with any dances with him, or any other jobs? No, no, no, never, never, never played with him. No. And, uh... By the way, the first time I met Jelly Roll was in Washington, D.C., about 1938 or 37. And, I began talking, asking like I talked to you. I didn't have a tape recorder, I'm sorry to say. But, I asked him about the different musicians. And, your name came up. I said, what about Mitchell? He's greater than Armstrong, he said. He meant it, too. He wasn't just talking, he meant it. He liked you better than Armstrong. And, he said Simeon was his favorite clarinet player. Well, that Simeon, I liked him. He was great. He was great. He's great. He's still great. He's still playing. Is he still... In New York, yes. He is, yeah. A friend of mine heard him about two weeks ago. Is that so? Down in New Orleans, said he'd heard him a week before in New York. He's still going. Yeah, I hadn't seen him or heard him. I've seen him for years. If he could tell something about how those records were made, did you rehearse them?
